topic.name: EGFR-mutant lung cancer: resistance to osimertinib
topic.question: New evidence on how EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer becomes resistant to osimertinib, how often each mechanism occurs, and what works after resistance.
topic.primary_query: (EGFR[tiab] OR "ErbB Receptors"[mh]) AND (osimertinib[tiab] OR AZD9291[tiab] OR Tagrisso[tiab]) AND resistan*[tiab]
topic.secondary_query: ("Drug Resistance, Neoplasm"[mh] OR "acquired resistance"[tiab] OR "disease progression"[tiab] OR progressed[tiab]) AND ("third-generation"[tiab] OR "third generation"[tiab] OR T790M[tiab] OR C797S[tiab] OR "EGFR-TKI"[tiab] OR "EGFR TKI"[tiab]) AND (NSCLC[tiab] OR "lung cancer"[tiab] OR "lung adenocarcinoma"[tiab])

criteria.text: Concerns EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: patients, tumour samples, cell lines or animal models.
Involves osimertinib (also called AZD9291 or Tagrisso), alone or in combination.
Reports on resistance to osimertinib: a mechanism, how often a mechanism occurs, or treatment after resistance.
Reports original data (trial, cohort, case report, laboratory study) rather than being only a review, editorial or guideline.

fields.text: The resistance mechanism the paper describes, genetic or not, in the paper's words, e.g. MET amplification, ERK/GATAD2A/SAA1 axis, histological transformation.
Specific genetic alteration(s) reported, as written in the paper, e.g. EGFR C797S, MET amplification. Null if the mechanism is not a genetic alteration.
Context of the alteration, e.g. in cis or in trans with T790M, co-occurring alterations.
Treatment line or setting, e.g. first-line osimertinib, after progression.
Study design, e.g. retrospective cohort, phase 2 trial, case report, cell-line study.
Number of patients, if stated. Digits only.
What kind of finding the paper reports. Exactly one of the allowed values.
The main result in one sentence, staying as close to the paper's wording as possible.

high_impact.why: A result on what to give after resistance can change treatment, so a person always reads it. Mechanism papers are checked like any other and reach a person when a check fails.

paper.title: Reversal of acquired osimertinib resistance by YAP inhibition in lung cancer is associated with lipid metabolic reprogramming.
paper.abstract: Osimertinib (Osi), as the third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI), has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, recent studies have found that its acquired resistance severely limits its therapeutic effect. This study shows that YAP activation is associated with lipid metabolic reprogramming in Osi-acquired resistance, providing new insights into overcoming this clinical challenge. In H1975/OR cells, YAP phosphorylation was decreased and nuclear translocation was increased, indicating YAP activation. Inhibition or knockdown of YAP significantly re-stored Osi sensitivity. YAP upregulated the expression of sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), fatty acid synthase (FASN), and stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD1), and promoted the synthesis of triglycerides, cholesterol, and phospholipids. Lipidomics revealed that YAP inhibition reduced multiple phospholipids. Furthermore, inhibition of YAP downregulated the anti-apoptotic protein B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL2) and enhanced Osi-induced apoptosis. This study firstly links YAP activation to lipid metabolic reprogramming and reveals its crucial role in Osi-acquired resistance. These findings not only deepen the understanding of the EGFR-TKI resistance mechanism but also provide a new therapeutic strategy for clinically overcoming Osi-acquired resistance. Targeting the phospholipid synthesis pathway mediated by YAP may effectively reverse the acquired resistance of NSCLC to Osi.

paper.title: Overcoming EGFR Resistance by Monovalent and Bident Inhibitors Targeting Cys775.
paper.abstract: Covalent targeting of EGFR cysteine 797 by osimertinib is one of the most successful breakthroughs in targeted therapy, fundamentally transforming the treatment landscape for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. However, resistance driven by the mutation of C797 remains a major clinical challenge. Developing novel covalent strategies beyond C797 targeting presents a compelling opportunity for next-generation EGFR inhibitors. We first demonstrated that cysteine 775, located deep within the ATP-binding pocket, is accessible by a rationally designed covalent molecule ZNL-3, which as the first-in-class covalent cysteine 775 inhibitor exhibited strong efficacy in osimertinib-resistant mouse models. To further enhance resilience to resistance-causing mutations, we developed a dual-warhead, bident compound YNW-1 which covalently targets both cysteines 775 and 797 simultaneously. YNW-1 is the first intramolecular lock to exhibit balanced reactive efficiency on both cysteines, rendering single-site mutations ineffective at conferring resistance. This study establishes the therapeutic potential of an EGFR covalent inhibitor through unprecedented targeting of cysteine 775. It also provides the first evidence that dual-cysteine engagement offers superior efficacy to conventional covalent inhibitors by delaying the emergence of resistance. Further optimization for clinical translation is currently ongoing in our laboratory.

paper.title: Long-term Disease Control After Probable Endobronchial Small-cell Transformation During Osimertinib Therapy for EGFR-mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma.
paper.abstract: Background/aim: Osimertinib provides durable progression-free survival in EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance is inevitable. Histologic transformation to small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a recognized resistance mechanism, typically presenting with widespread metastatic disease and a poor prognosis. Optimal post-transformation treatment strategies have not been established. Case report: We report a patient with EGFR exon 19 deletion-positive lung adenocarcinoma who achieved prolonged disease control on osimertinib for mediastinal lymph node recurrence before developing a new endobronchial lesion in the left main bronchus. Rigid bronchoscopic resection and temporary airway stenting relieved the critical obstruction. Pathologic examination confirmed SCLC, and immunohistochemistry of both the initial adenocarcinoma and the endobronchial lesion demonstrated concordant p53 over-expression and loss of Rb expression, supporting a clinical diagnosis of probable histologic transformation. The patient was bridged to sequential chemoradiotherapy, followed by successful stent removal and the resumption of osimertinib, resulting in long-term disease control exceeding four years. Conclusion: An individualized, multidisciplinary approach comprising rigid bronchoscopic resection, temporary airway stenting, chemoradiotherapy, and osimertinib resumption may achieve prolonged disease control in locoregionally confined SCLC arising during osimertinib therapy. Further case accumulation is warranted to establish optimal treatment strategies.

paper.title: Simultaneous occurrence of HER2 mutation and PD-L1 high expression in EGFR-mutant NSCLC: a case report.
paper.abstract: In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), EGFR and HER2 mutations are generally considered mutually exclusive events, with a co-occurrence probability estimated to be less than 1%. Patients with either EGFR or HER2 mutations tend to exhibit low PD-L1 expression levels. The simultaneous presence of both EGFR and HER2 mutations accompanied by high PD-L1 expression is exceedingly rare. This study reports a female patient who was admitted to the hospital after a routine physical examination revealed a right lung nodule and was diagnosed with "right lung adenocarcinoma (cT2aN2aM1c1, IVA; EGFR 21 L858R mutation; HER2 exon 8 mutation; PD-L1 TPS 60%)." The patient was immediately started on first-line third-generation EGFR-targeted therapy (Furmonertinib), but disease progression occurred after just 4.4 months (malignant pleural effusion and pericardial effusion). As the patient refused repeat biopsy, treatment with an ADC drug (Trastuzumab rezetecan) was initiated. Disease control was achieved after only one cycle of treatment, and the regimen was continued thereafter. The progression-free survival has exceeded 5.3 months, and at the time of writing this report, the disease remained well-controlled. This paper presents the first report of this rare and therapeutically challenging combination of molecular pathological features-concurrent EGFR and HER2 mutations with high PD-L1 expression in an NSCLC patient. When standard first-line third-generation EGFR-TKIs proved ineffective, the successful use of an anti-HER2 ADC drug to control the tumor demonstrates its potential clinical value. However, whether all patients initially presenting with this pathological molecular subtype will achieve consistent efficacy remains to be further investigated.

paper.title: Genomic landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance: from known mechanisms to unknown resistance.
paper.abstract: Purpose: Epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) serve as the standard first-line therapy for advanced EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, resistance inevitably restricts their efficacy. Although well-documented acquired resistance mechanisms have been extensively characterized, approximately 30% of patients with EGFR-TKI resistance still present with unknown resistance (UR) mechanisms, and the driving factors behind primary resistance remain inadequately understood. Methods: In this study, we conducted a large-scale, retrospective cohort study, performing target-capture deep sequencing (>400 genes) on 928 samples from 745 EGFR-TKI-resistant and 183 TKI-naïve EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Results: The molecular landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance was systematically characterized. In the resistance cohort, 68.72% (512/745) harbored known resistance (KR) mechanisms, while 31.28% (233/745) were classified as UR. The landscape of KR was significantly influenced by EGFR-TKI generation. First-line third-generation TKI resistance demonstrated fewer EGFR-dependent events compared to first-generation TKIs (p < 0.01) and more RTK and PI3K-AKT-mTOR (PAM) pathway alterations (p < 0.05). In the UR cohort, pathway analysis revealed unique enrichment of atypical pathways, most notably ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling pathways. Differential gene analysis identified significant enrichment of MYC, BRCA1, EPHB, and PTPRD in the UR subgroup. To investigate primary resistance, we found that baseline IKZF1 amplification was significantly enriched in patients with short time-to-treatment-failure (TTF) and correlated with significantly poorer outcomes (HR = 3.02, 95% CI 1.32-6.90; log-rank p = 0.004). Conclusions: This study provides a comprehensive real-world landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance, demonstrating distinct mechanisms influenced by TKI generation. ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling was identified as a distinctive pathway feature of unknown resistance, and baseline IKZF1 amplification emerged as a candidate biomarker of EGFR-TKI primary resistance. These findings suggest that epigenetic dysregulation may be a critical driver of both unknown and primary resistance to EGFR-TKIs.

summary.text: In a retrospective cohort of 928 patients with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC receiving first-line EGFR-TKIs, ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling was identified as a distinctive pathway feature of unknown resistance. Additionally, baseline IKZF1 amplification emerged as a candidate biomarker for primary resistance to these therapies.

claims.evidence: In the UR cohort, pathway analysis revealed unique enrichment of atypical pathways, most notably ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling pathways.

To investigate primary resistance, we found that baseline IKZF1 amplification was significantly enriched in patients with short time-to-treatment-failure (TTF) and correlated with significantly poorer outcomes (HR = 3.02, 95% CI 1.32-6.90; log-rank p = 0.004).
